review_items.title: 'Outlet' proposed for every unit whose permit lists the stream's codes: count a permitted unit as an available outlet whatever its bookings?
review_items.detail: The permit table says which codes a unit may take; the bookings say whether it can in the week. Accepting the proposal would make 'outlet' mean 'permitted somewhere', so Port Terrell (94% booked and down since 3 November) would read as an outlet for the Halden process water and for the fourteen stranded manifests, and the acceptance policy's capacity test (section 4) would be lost.

actions.label: Keep permitted and available distinct: an outlet needs capacity in the period
Create a state 'outlet = permitted for the codes'

evidence: Waste_Acceptance_Policy_2025.pdf section 4: a permitted code is not an outlet by itself
ops.capacity_booking: Port Terrell aqueous incineration 94.4% booked for the fourth quarter; weeks 45 and 46 flagged outage
Thread F1: Elena Vasquez, kiln down from 3 November

review_items.title: H1 process wastewater → Bayou Verde deep well proposed as meeting the destruction requirement, with a certificate of disposal in place of a certificate of destruction?
review_items.detail: Deep well is the cheapest permitted route for the stream and the UIC permit lets Bayou Verde issue a certificate of disposal. QR-14 asks for destruction by incineration with a certificate of destruction per shipment, and Halden's quality team rejected deep well at two other plants. Approving the link would quote a route the customer requirement rules out.
evidence: Halden_Quality_Requirement_QR-14_Waste_Destruction.pdf: deep well, landfill and treatment for discharge are not acceptable
Bayou_Verde_UIC_Permit_Summary.pdf: disposal, not destruction
Thread A2: Priya Natarajan, Halden quality rejected deep well

review_items.title: Port Terrell's fourth-quarter booking proposed as its first-quarter 2027 plan for the Halden routing?
review_items.detail: Port Terrell has not published a first-quarter plan; its fourth quarter is 94% booked and the committee ruled out new pharmaceutical volume there until the plan is out. Accepting would present a repeat of the fourth quarter as a plan and let the Halden process water be quoted on capacity nobody has confirmed.

actions.label: Keep the first quarter unplanned; cost Port Terrell at the alternative
Treat the fourth-quarter booking as the first-quarter plan

evidence: Capacity_Plan_Q4_2026.xlsx: Port Terrell has not submitted a first-quarter plan
Capacity_Committee_Q3_2026_minutes.pdf item 2
Thread A1: Dana Whitfield, quote on Granger unless Port Terrell publishes a plan

review_items.title: The 578 LegacyTrack profiles and their mirrors in the operations system: same profiles, merge and count as approved?
review_items.detail: Each legacy profile has a mirror marked legacy. Merging would count unreviewed profiles with the acquired companies' prices as approved Ironbridge profiles, and change the approved count, the expiring count and the margin by facility for the East business.
evidence: legacy.legacy_profile.reviewed: false on every row
Thread P1: Owen Pratt, not to be counted as approved
LegacyTrack_Migration_Status_2026-10.pdf: migration from January 2027

review_items.title: Meridian West → APPROVES the two Gulf overflow profiles after 30 November, because the outlet is still on the register?
review_items.detail: The outlet stays on the register; the approvals on the two profiles expire 30 November and renewal is at a higher price with re-approval. Approving the link past the date would keep an expired approval as an outlet, which the acceptance policy (section 7) rules out.
evidence: Third_Party_Outlet_Approvals_Register_2026-10.xlsx: two overflow approvals to 30 November
Meridian_West_Approval_Letter_2026-09-02.pdf: renewal subject to the 2027 price list and re-approval
Thread F3: Carla Dimitriou

review_items.title: The 1 November Illinois fee rise proposed as billed on every Riverbend contract from the next invoice?
review_items.detail: The pricing policy passes a fee through only where the contract carries clause 9.2. Two Riverbend stabilization contracts do not; billing the rise on them would be a price change without a contract basis, and leaving them as they are puts them under the stream floor.

actions.label: Keep pass-through to contracts with clause 9.2; flag the two without it
Bill the rise on every Riverbend contract

evidence: Pricing_and_Margin_Policy_2026.pdf section 6: pass-through where the contract carries clause 9.2
fin.state_fee: Illinois $13.50 to $16.50 from 1 November
Thread B1: Raj Mehta, two contracts without the clause

review_items.title: Halden Biopharma → CAN_SHIP once its six profiles are approved, before the EPA identification number is issued?
review_items.detail: Approval of a profile says the waste is understood and has an outlet; a manifest needs the generator's EPA identification number. Halden has applied and has no number yet. Approving the link would let the quote imply shipments can start on signature.
evidence: ops.generator.epa_id: empty for G11100
Thread E1: Linda Choi, no manifest moves until the number is issued
Halden_Waste_Profiles_2026-10-22.xlsx: applied for, not yet issued

review_items.title: Granger aqueous incineration → CAN_RECEIVE the Galena Shores loads before Walt Brennan confirms the slots?
review_items.detail: The bookings show headroom at Granger in weeks 45 and 46 (336 tons of aqueous), and Walt Brennan's mail gives about the same figure. The link is derived from the bookings; the slots still need the plant manager to confirm before the trucks are booked.
evidence: ops.capacity_booking: Granger weeks 45 and 46
Thread R1: Walt Brennan, send me the list and I will confirm the slots
Thread R2: Hector Ruiz, first loads Thursday

pivot.title: 'Outlet' proposed for every unit whose permit lists the stream's codes: count a permitted unit as an available outlet whatever its bookings?
pivot.detail: The permit table says which codes a unit may take; the bookings say whether it can in the week. Accepting the proposal would make 'outlet' mean 'permitted somewhere', so Port Terrell (94% booked and down since 3 November) would read as an outlet for the Halden process water and for the fourteen stranded manifests, and the acceptance policy's capacity test (section 4) would be lost.
pivot.why_pivot: This item changes what a word means, not what a row says. Accepting it silently would make every answer about outlets and routing count a permitted unit as available whatever its bookings, so the Halden quote, the stranded manifests and the capacity board would all look safer than the records support.
evidence: Waste_Acceptance_Policy_2025.pdf section 4: a permitted code is not an outlet by itself
ops.capacity_booking: Port Terrell aqueous incineration 94.4% booked for the fourth quarter; weeks 45 and 46 flagged outage
Thread F1: Elena Vasquez, kiln down from 3 November

options.label: Keep permitted and available distinct: an outlet needs capacity in the period
options.consequence: Answers test every route against the bookings of the receiving unit for the weeks it would arrive; a permitted unit without capacity is shown as permitted, not as an outlet.

options.label: Create a state 'outlet = permitted for the codes'
options.consequence: Adds a state; Port Terrell then counts as an outlet for every stream its permit lists, including while it is down, and routing stops reconciling to the bookings.

sanity_checks.question: What is booked against the capacity of each incineration unit, and what headroom is left in November?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - from the bookings, week by week
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Unit -> booked against permitted -> the capacity condition. Headroom is capacity minus booked for the weeks asked; an outage week has none (rq1).

context.label: a permitted code is not an outlet

sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (u:Unit)-[:HAS_MEASURE]->(m:Measure {id:'booked-vs-permitted'})
MATCH (h:Measure {id:'unit-headroom'})-[:TESTED_AGAINST]->(c:Condition {id:'outlet_capacity'})
RETURN u, m, h, c

sanity_checks.question: What would the six Halden streams earn a year by route, at the price book, on full cost?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - full cost at every permitted route, price book, margin floor
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Quote -> stream -> routes -> the margin measure -> the floor condition. Routes a requirement rules out are shown and not quoted; Port Terrell is costed at the alternative (rq3).

context.label: full cost at the quoted routing

sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (q:Quote {id:'Q-2026-0141'})<-[:LINE_OF]-(p:Profile)<-[:ROUTES]-(r:Route)
MATCH (r)-[:HAS_MEASURE]->(m:Measure {id:'stream-margin'})-[:TESTED_AGAINST]->(c:Condition {id:'margin_floor'})
RETURN p, r, m, c

sanity_checks.question: What does the Port Terrell outage strand, and where can each shipment go?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - open manifests against the outage weeks and the other units' headroom
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Outage -> stopped units -> manifests booked at them -> units that can receive them. A hold at a service center is tested against its ten-day clock; a truck's position is not available.
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (o:Outage)-[:STOPS]->(u:Unit)<-[:BOOKED_AT]-(m:Manifest)
OPTIONAL MATCH (g:Unit)-[:CAN_RECEIVE]->(m)
RETURN o, u, m, g

sanity_checks.question: Which of the six Halden streams meet the destruction requirement at which units, and which outlets are ruled out by it?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - the requirement binds the routing
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Profile -> SUBJECT_TO the destruction condition -> routes that FAIL it. Deep well, landfill and discharge treatment are shown as ruled out, with the reason (rq2).
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (p:Profile)-[:SUBJECT_TO]->(c:Condition {id:'destruction'})
MATCH (r:Route)-[:ROUTES]->(p)
OPTIONAL MATCH (r)-[:FAILS]->(x:Condition)
RETURN p, r, x
